newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen sees 250 mln stg p/a from new deals.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen sees 250 mln stg p/a from new deals.

text.p: PowerGen, Britain's second biggest electricity generator, said on Tuesday it expected new businesses to contribute around 250 million pounds per year to trading profits by 2003.

Deryk King, PowerGen's group managing director, told analysts that three recently announced international power projects in Thailand, Indonesia and Hungary were estimated to add 200 million pounds per year to trading profits when they were up and running in 2003.

Contributions from its portfolio of upstream gas and oil assets, PowerGen North Sea Ltd, and PowerGen CHP Ltd (combined heat and power plants) would take trading profits from new business operations towards 250 million stg per year, the company added in a statement.
PowerGen is taking a 40 percent stake in a coal-fired project at Serang in Indonesia and a 30 percent stake in a 1400 megawatt coal-fired plant at Map Ta Phut in Thailand.
The company also plans to build a modern, high efficiency 390 megawatt gas-fired plant on the site of its existing wholly-owned 43 megawatt Csepel plant in Budapest, Hungary.

The addition of these three new projects gives PowerGen interests in more than 7700 megawatt of gross generating capacity and takes the group's equity commitments in international power projects to around 700 million pounds, the group said last month.
PowerGen's remaining new business operations comprise its North Sea Ltd business and CHP Ltd.

Operating profits from its upstream gas and oil assets rose to 15 million stg in the year to March 1997 and are set to grow as oil and gas production from the Liverpool Bay development builds to peak levels and phase two of the Galleon field development is brought on stream.

Four CHP projects last year also started to contribute to operating profits. A fifth -- a plant that will supply the electricity and steam requirements of DuPont Co's Conoco (UK) Humber refinery -- is on course to be fully operational by the summer.

Construction of PowerGen's biggest CHP project -- for Brunner Mond (UK) Ltd -- will begin later this year. The value of PowerGen's committed investments in the CHP business is 250 million pounds. Three further projects are being progressed on an exclusive basis, the company said in May.
